reviews.text: I'm incredibly grateful to have found the clinic and Dr. Corso in particular: after an emergency hospitalization, she remained my trusted veterinarian, the only one I've found in Milan with empathy and attention to the real needs of my dogs, without trying to sell me useless services for the well-being of my four-legged friends, as many unfortunately do lately.
The nurse who performed the cardiac ultrasound on my cat was very thorough and attentive. My advice: don't fast while your cat undergoes the blood tests, as this makes the exam more difficult.
Very, very good. Excellent staff. We had a great time with our dachshund, from the first moment!!!!

Last night (Sunday, almost 11:00 PM and close to closing time), we found ourselves in a very urgent situation. Our dog had been suffering from severe diarrhea for two days, worsening, and had recently started vomiting. We were very hesitant to go to the emergency room given the hour, but we decided to call. Dr. Anfray Pascal answered and, after carefully listening to her symptoms, told us to take her in immediately for an evaluation.
Thank goodness we listened. Not only did the doctor promptly treat and restore our dog's health, but we were fortunate to meet an exceptional professional. Over the past six years, we've visited countless veterinary clinics, and for the first time, we've met a doctor who is not only extremely reliable, but also honest, empathetic, and deeply human.
Knowing we can turn to him to address our doubts and concerns without the fear of receiving a snarky response (as had unfortunately often happened to us elsewhere) is invaluable. I don't usually write reviews, but I know how frustrating and stressful it is to search for a good vet based solely on reviews online. This time, I had to share my experience to help other pet owners.
If you go to Cribiori Veterinary Clinic, ask for Dr. Anfray Pascal. Trust me, you won't regret entrusting your pets to him. After meeting him, we know we've finally found a trustworthy vet we'll be happy to turn to again.
I went to them because of an ear of corn stuck in my dog's ear. The doctor immediately examined him under sedation and removed the ear of corn. He was very quick and competent!

I discovered and used this emergency veterinary clinic for my brother-in-law's dog. We were welcomed, and shortly after, the dog was thoroughly examined by a wonderful doctor, who treated him for a lesion on the back of one leg and administered an anti-inflammatory injection for the pain.
This occurred on May 16th at 9:45 PM, after we took the dog to the veterinary clinic on Via Donatello, where we were told they could only examine the dog around 5:00 AM. They therefore advised us to return the next day.
We found the aforementioned emergency clinic by chance, having searched online for the dog's condition, and they took us there, where the dog was promptly treated.
If you need an efficient emergency veterinary clinic, consider the one on Via Melchiorre Gioia 67.
Highly recommended for the professionalism and thoroughness with which the dog was treated.

A truly excellent experience. They treated my dog ​​after he had been to another clinic and they couldn't get him to do anything. There the doctor did all the tests and x-rays on my dog ​​and immediately identified the problem, treated him as best as possible and now he, even at 16 years old, is doing very well. Thank you very much.

We took our cat to the clinic twice for cystitis. The first time, he was sent home, underestimating his condition. The second time, however, after tests and investigations, a significantly overdose of medication was prescribed, causing the cat even more problems, in addition to those already identified. The risk we were exposed to was significant, and fortunately, we were able to transfer them to another clinic. The cat has now recovered from poorly managed cystitis and is doing well.
Furthermore, we had to repeatedly request the reports and analyses from the visits via email.
For 1 minute visit 60€ telling me little or nothing

Honestly, I didn't have a great experience. The doctor on the phone said he dealt with rats, so my boyfriend and I brought my rat. The visit lasted a mere two seconds, and without even taking her out of the carrier, he said she was "breathing fine." I'm not a doctor, but any vet listens to her lungs before making that statement, especially about a rat. He literally didn't know how to handle them; my little one was wriggling and whining in an absurd way, obviously because he had little experience, or at least little training. In short, a two-minute visit for €60, saying "he didn't charge us for the emergency room time." I don't recommend it for rats, but I don't know about other animals. Anyway, he was polite; I felt a little unwell, so he made me lie down on a bed and gave me some water.

A terrible experience. Last night, Saturday, May 30, 2026, I called to bring my young and healthy dog ​​to have a foxtail removed from her ear. When we arrived, there was only one "vet" who attempted to remove the foxtail, with the dog, as she herself said, extremely cooperative. She was unsuccessful; she told me she would have to sedate her. After sedation, she repeatedly attempted intravenous access, and by her own admission, she said she wasn't capable. Meanwhile, the dog was bleeding and her leg was swollen. She didn't remove the foxtail, but a piece of earwax, claiming it was part of the foreign body.
We had to go to another clinic where the health of the dog, who was very debilitated and in pain, needed to be assessed.
It is neither professional nor ethically correct to proceed by trial and error on the skin of a living being.

I've been coming to this veterinary clinic for almost twenty years, both for emergencies and for routine checkups and treatments. I've always found the most appropriate answers and treatments for my dogs, with a focus on sustainability and testing to avoid excessive suffering for my beloved dogs.

Very bad experience, my dog ​​arrived dehydrated, they gave her a 30 second drip and then sent her home, after 1 hour my dog ​​went into shock, however they made me pay 120 euros, thank goodness I took her to a serious vet, not this one who also works in pajamas at 10 in the morning
The best veterinary staff for professionalism, courtesy and availability...Dr. Cribiori is truly a great professional....they operated on my Labrador and everything was perfect. Thank you so much

Appointment at 9:00. We found a vacuum! No one was there, nor was anyone answering the phone, just a voicemail saying the emergency room is closed until 9:00 on March 9th. After a forty-minute wait, we left! Congratulations!

AWFUL EXPERIENCE!!!!!! DON'T BE FOOLED BY THE 4.3 SCORE.
I went to the emergency vet on Sunday with my dachshund. Abdominal pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. We waited over three hours, had tests that proved useless, and paid €400. As I looked shocked by the price, considering I would have taken the dog home in the same condition, the doctor on duty immediately became annoyed, losing all professionalism in a matter of seconds and raising her voice significantly. Terrible!
Not only that, for most of the visit, during delicate moments like blood sampling or IV administration, I had to hold the dog, without knowing how not to hurt him if he made sudden movements. The response I was given was, "He's your dog, you know how to calm him down." This is all true, but there were two of them, and no clinic I've ever been to during such delicate phases would let the owner participate, with the risk of hurting the dog.
The gentleman who was with this completely incompetent doctor had to tare the scale three times because he didn't realize he was standing on it. In the end, I did it myself.
NEVER AGAIN, NEVER AGAIN!
Finally, to close things off, the place was very dirty. We entered the examination room and there were still blood samples thrown into bowls belonging to dogs that had come before mine.

I thank all the medical staff who cared for my little cat. Although he didn't survive his illness, I truly thank with all my heart all the wonderful doctors who did everything they could to save him. Many thanks to Dr. Corso, Dr. Croce, and the magnificent Dr. Cribiori. You made my Ragù's last days very sweet. Thank you, thank you for your humanity and professionalism.
Available and professional

I sincerely thank the staff at this clinic and emergency room (going down the stairs on the left!) for their hospitality, promptness, and professionalism. They saved my cat Benjie from certain death within days, if I had continued to trust a veterinarian at another practice who completely failed to diagnose a gastrointestinal condition, which quickly worsened despite several symptoms clearly visible to the expert eye. A shocking lack of skill and professionalism. At this clinic, Benjie was entrusted in particular to the care of Dr. Veronica Corso, to whom I am deeply grateful and whom I would like to thank again for her attention and dedication, as well as for her undoubted clinical expertise in healing my cat, despite a truly critical situation.
5 stars… but the love that Dr. Cribiori transmitted to my old Bracco deserves many, many more!!!

I was calling and asking if we can come tonight because we have an emergency with our dog. It was 5pm and they said no, we have to make an appointment and NOT FOR TODAY.  Yes it was said in First Aid clinic . Crazy.
Dr. Veronica is the best and most friendly. Thank you, Doctor.

From the moment you arrive, you understand that love for dogs doesn't exist here, leaving aside the arrogance of the girl at the reception... they ask you to wait an hour to cut a couple of nails for my dog, dwarf...

A well-equipped clinic, with doctors who are always available and patient. Dr. Cribiori is an extraordinary professional: his kindness and the attention he gives to animals always move me. A heartfelt thank you to the entire team for the passion and love you bring to your work. 💙🐾 …

I am infinitely grateful to Dr. Cribiori and the other veterinarians at the clinic for these two months of therapy and care. Although Loki is sadly no longer with us, they directed me to ensure that the short time he had left with us was of an acceptable quality, avoiding the aggressive treatment that an inexperienced human companion who cannot accept suffering might seek. Instead, they, with professionalism and empathy, were able to put a stop to my suffering, and I thank them for that. We never want to experience the end of our lives when it comes to those we love... but sometimes you just have to accept it and support them in the best possible way... Loki had a fairly dignified end, despite what was unfortunately a disease that took him. I am grateful for the availability, sincerity, efficiency, and above all, the humanity I encountered in Dr. Cribiori and his staff.

I took my cat in at night because she was very ill. She was emaciated and dehydrated due to an unknown illness. I've been to so many vets, and no one could tell me what was wrong.
The vet did all the checks, but he kept saying the prognosis was guarded. It got to the point where I had to put the cat down so she wouldn't suffer any more because she was very ill.
The vet in question even charged 10 euros more than expected.

I had my kitten vaccinated, and the doctor also gave her a complete checkup. She was very kind and found my kitten to be in excellent health.

Thank you, doctor.

To keep in mind...
We came to this „24/7” vet because we had an emergency at 4:50 on a Wednesday, but it was in fact not open.
Excellent service, cat well cared for. Now the convalescence is over, on the road to recovery.
Professional and attentive

I took my 5-month-old kitten to the hospital last night. The doctor was very kind and helpful, but he sent me home after treatment with suspicion of parvovirus. This suspicion was confirmed two hours later by another emergency room, where I took the practically dying kitten. At the second center (and then the third, where he is now hospitalized), they were very surprised that he had been released.

On the 23rd at 9:00 AM, I took my cat to the clinic, and on the 27th I was informed that he had died. In just four days, he was given three anesthesia treatments. On the 27th, around 1:00 PM, he was given further sedation, which resulted in cardiac arrest. At 2:00 PM, they called me to tell me that my cat had died.

It was just a minor operation for kidney stones; I can't understand why, in the space of four days, they deemed it necessary to administer three anesthesia treatments and a sedative. Not even an adult human could tolerate such a pharmacological burden, let alone a four-year-old cat.

It's clear that there was no attention paid to his health. They didn't even consider whether he was still able to tolerate further sedation. Their negligence led to my cat's death. It's unacceptable.
A highly specialized team. My Pomeranian underwent minor surgery to remove a foreign body from his eye very quickly and with the utmost care. Thanks to Dr. Veronica Corso and her team.

My dog ​​had been sick for a week and was getting worse. I called Dr. Cribiori, who immediately advised me. He provided a timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment. I found him to be competent and kind. For this, I thank him and highly recommend him.

Today I took my dog ​​to their emergency room urgently due to an allergic reaction (hives all over her body, swollen ears/muzzle, and labored breathing). I called around 7:00 a.m., and we were there half an hour later. The doctor was very welcoming, professional, and kind. He immediately examined her, administered the necessary injections, and prescribed the antibiotic, giving me further instructions and explaining the situation thoroughly. In total, I paid €130, which I think is very good for the service provided.
He saw the cat right away, late in the evening. The vet was excellent, very kind and helpful.

A complete lack of professionalism and competence, cloaked in a veneer of good manners, but it was only a veneer, given the stupidity and ignorance of the comments added at the top. Evidently, there's also a difficulty understanding the Italian language: I wished my poor cat hadn't suffered needlessly or had a real chance of survival, a chance he perhaps would have had if this emergency room had had a real oxygen cage, or if the guy on the phone had told me no, they didn't have a real oxygen cage. Here are the facts:
The owner, I think, answered and told me he had an oxygen cage. The next day I saw some real oxygen cages—in the clinic where I transferred the cat—and they were very different from the collapsible plastic box, full of cracks and holes, into which he placed two thin tubes with oxygen, assuring me that leakage wouldn't be a problem. He kept the cat in there for a few hours and charged me the equivalent of a day's hospitalization. According to every other vet I spoke with, the oxygen cage was essential for treating the cat with heart problems and severe breathing difficulties, and he should have been left there until he improved. My colleague had warned me over the phone that the cat's condition had worsened, while the owner maintained that he was stable. I don't know if the cat would have survived if he had received the appropriate treatment immediately, because his condition was serious, but despite being transferred to a real oxygen cage, he continued to deteriorate and died the following morning. Perhaps things would have gone more or less the same way, but I would have preferred more clarity and professionalism. Not recommended for serious problems, and that's the main reason I wrote this review, in the hope it will be useful for other cats and dogs.
Now that anyone can be so vulgar and humanly ignorant as to quote the farewell words used after the loss speaks volumes about the person who wrote that shameful and insulting comment, a truly ignorant person! If you love your pets: TAKE THEM ELSEWHERE. I'd add that the vet across the street, a very good vet, if he happened to close in the meantime, would have done so both because he's retired and because of the defamation he's received from the supposed emergency room across the street, which, moreover: STINKS! Because they clean poorly and poorly! And if you have any doubts about this, just flare your nostrils when you arrive. After that, you'd better turn around and go elsewhere!

PS. I see you have no shame! All the doctors I spoke to told me that oxygen was essential, and the owner said it wasn't necessary for him to be on oxygen all the time and in a cage without leaks! And you kept him there for only a few hours—you pay about double what you pay in other clinics with REAL oxygen cages!!!
Is this heart???
Your only concern is maintaining a false image! By shifting the blame onto the neighbor and sending injured animals home (in other cases)—as I've read in several reviews!

You would have been better off keeping quiet.
I repeat: it's HIGHLY not recommended for anyone with critically ill animals!

Sunday evening at 11:00 pm, I showed up unannounced with a newly caught stray cat. The doctor was very kind and helpful, the chip scan (negative) and the consultation (half an hour) on what to do next were free, courteous, and clear.
Thank you 💟 …

Our dog is sick tonight. We went to this emergency veterinary clinic, as we've done in the past. We tried calling first, but no one answered. Not even a pre-recorded message. We went anyway, and after ringing the bell twice, they answered and said "the emergency clinic is closed"??!!? Why not put up a notice? It wasn't marked on Google Maps, where it said it was open, nor on the answering machine, nor on the signs outside the building.... Well done.
Thank you 💟 …

Terrible! They advertise that they're open 24 hours a day, but if you go at 3 in the morning, after ringing the doorbell three times, a vet who looks like a security guard answers and tells you they don't have the equipment to examine my dog... it's shameful.
THEY DON'T ANSWER!
24/7, not at all. It's closed at midnight.

I brought my dog ​​in Sunday morning, and he was collapsed.
The doctor didn't even do an X-ray. He said he had a sore throat.
Today I spent a day at the San Siro Veterinary Clinic with my dog, who has pulmonary edema!!
Highly not recommended!!!!

Superb emergency care for four-legged friends! There's never a long wait, they always answer the phone, they have extremely competitive prices, and they're very knowledgeable and professional! Better than many other clinics in the area, trust me!
A doctor with great experience.

Terrible.... half an hour outside the closed door even if it is written in front of the bell on the phone and on the intercom nobody answers IT IS NOT AN EMERGENCY ROOM let's rush to another and hope for the best VERY BAD
24/7, but despite several calls during the night, I have had no answer

The emergency room is located inside the building.
After passing through the main door and the hallway, the stairs are on the left.
The doctor is very kind; he greeted us immediately and examined our cat right away.
He ran all the necessary tests, prescribed and administered the necessary medication.
He reassured us and gave us all the necessary instructions.
Truly kind and competent.
If we need anything, we will definitely contact him again.
One star because it was closed on a Monday night, even though it was advertised as open. They didn't answer the phone.
Excellent emergency room. Clean, welcoming, and super fast.
Always our go-to for Joe for years. Thank you, Dr. Croce, for always being attentive. 👍 …
Professional and friendly as always. We've been going there for years.

UNACCEPTABLE experience.
We arrived at the emergency veterinary clinic with our pet at around 3:30 a.m. between Saturday and Sunday, and despite the critical situation, we were faced with a complete absurdity.
We rang three different intercoms for over 7 minutes, and no one—I repeat, NO ONE—deigned to answer. A surreal and disconcerting situation, especially for a place that should be ready to intervene at any moment, especially when an animal's life is in danger.
I would not recommend this place to anyone.
Shameful!

I called for help for my kitten who hasn't eaten for two days. A doctor answered rudely and hastily. I know the kitten's condition, but he insists they can't do anything because they don't follow her and the necessary tests would be expensive. I ask how much it is, and he says he doesn't know, it depends on the tests (so how can he say they would be expensive anyway). I insist because if she doesn't eat, she'll die, and he tells me there's nothing he can do and that he has a medical appointment to make. They shouldn't put animal "doctors" in the hands of certain people. Shameful.
Thanks

Congratulations to Dr. Cribiori. He carefully read the reports from the Bologna veterinarians and examined my cat for the first time.
He reassured me and didn't prescribe unnecessary tests or medications.
I highly recommend him.
The visits were very thorough

We had a great experience both with our dog at night and with our cat during the day. You always find different doctors, both male and female, but all are courteous and knowledgeable. I will always bring my dogs and cats here if needed. Prices are fair for a clinic, not excessive.
